ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, on the left is a 5 V DC power supply, connected through switch S to a series 10 µF capacitor; the node at the right end of the capacitor is connected through a 200 kΩ resistor to ground, and at the same time this node is sent into a sampler. The sampler is labeled fs = 10 Hz, the output sample is denoted as x(n), and it is then sent into the z-transform module. Reasoning: The switch is closed at t = 0^-, and sampling starts from t = 0. The capacitor is initially uncharged, so when the 5 V step is just applied, the initial value of the voltage at the upper end node of the resistor is 5 V; afterward it discharges through the 200 kΩ resistor and decays to 0. The time constant RC = 200 kΩ × 10 µF = 2 s, so the continuous-time output is x(t) = 5 e^{-t/2}. The sampling frequency is 10 Hz, therefore the sampling period Ts = 0.1 s. Let t = nTs = 0.1n, obtaining x(n) = 5 e^{-0.1n/2} = 5 e^{-0.05n}.

Since the capacitor is initially uncharged, the node voltage immediately after switching is 5 V, and it decays to zero with time constant RC=2 s.
